content.text: This wiki page recommends using fedora:status to do soft deletes:
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FF/Design+-+Deleting+Resources
I think fedora:status should be replaced with a different predicate, or moved to a different namespace if an appropriate existing predicate can't be found.
I agree with

. I'll go further (based on various conversations on the fedora-tech list and elsewhere) to say that Fedora itself shouldn't be managing this kind of state. This stuff is workflow-specific, and therefore application specific. Communities like Hydra or Islandora might support this kind of thing in some common way, but that's the lowest level of the stack on which it belongs.
There are two possible actions here:
1) Remove the #status predicate from the repository namespace. There is currently no internal use of that predicate. Do we plan on such a use?
2) Create a new Fedora vocabulary to host the #status predicate... unless there is a more standard term already in the wild.
Thoughts?
If not, we can take the third option: close this ticket and do nothing.

I think we should, at a minimum, remove the status predicate from the repository# ontology.  It cannot be used in the intended way, and we have no plans to add REST API functionality to manipulate it.

I would be find with creating a new ontology to house this predicate and the related values, if there are users who want to use them.  This is a carryover from fcrepo3, so I suspect there will be people migrating data who will want some standard way to express the fcrepo3 state for objects as they are migrated.  If there is an existing predicate, that would be preferable.
Is there an existing predicate in the Fedora 3 namespace or elsewhere that can be used for this purpose? Creating vocabularies for single terms does not sound very manageable... or attractive.
I believe fcrepo3 XML uses the element:
http://www.fedora.info/definitions/1/0/access/objState
That isn't deferenceable, so I don't know if there is an ontology defining it or not.
This is as close as we have to dereferencing/understanding #objState:
http://www.fedora.info/definitions/1/0/objectProfile.xsd
Let's talk about it on the Thursday call.
After further discussion, this task should:
1. Remove "status" related terms from the fedora/repository ontology
2. Create a dereferenceable resource at:
http://www.fedora.info/definitions/1/0/access/objState
Sorry, but I am unclear how I should achieve #2.
Actually publishing anything at that URL is definitely not something you can do without intervention from
, but you could write up whatever it is that should go at that location. Perhaps an RDFS document explaining `objState`?
, Could you create a new, small ontology document called "objState" that defines the "objState" property? I will then publish that resource so that the following will dereference:
http://www.fedora.info/definitions/1/0/access/objState
Please add this to the Thursday tech meeting agenda for discussion. There may be a better way??
Thoughts
My thoughts? See my comment above yours.
Okay, this is my
first attempt
to define a resource I'm going to let you all have your say before I submit a PR.
Also, do we want this part of the HTML reference build?
Please make a PR of this,
so others can review.
https://github.com/fcrepo4/ontology/pull/23
Resolved with:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/ontology/commit/88766107f78a5d7fd1ebc3044142ea9034617e61
When you try to update the fedora:status property, you get this error:
Ldp::HttpError: STATUS: 409 Could not persist triple containing predicate
http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/repository#status
This is because properties in the fedora: namespace are not user-modifiable.  So we need to move the property to a different namespace, or provide a mechanism for updating it in the REST API.

renderedFields.description:
When you try to update the fedora:status property, you get this error:

Ldp::HttpError: STATUS: 409 Could not persist triple containing predicate http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/repository#status

This is because properties in the fedora: namespace are not user-modifiable. So we need to move the property to a different namespace, or provide a mechanism for updating it in the REST API.
